athena.directive: Establish the Creative Liberation Engine as a fully autonomous, self-improving design and development entity capable of generating sophisticated, aesthetically pleasing, and highly functional user interfaces and landing pages from conceptual prompts, adhering strictly to constitutional principles of sovereignty and quality.
athena.rationale: The ability to autonomously design and build its own interfaces is fundamental to the Creative Liberation Engine's self-sufficiency and its mission to eliminate human wait time. Relying on external 'skills' or frameworks like 'Hallmark' violates Article I (Sovereignty) and introduces external dependencies, preventing complete ownership and control. This directive ensures the Creative Liberation Engine develops its own internal, robust, and high-quality UI/UX generation capabilities, aligning with Article IV (Quality Standards) and Article IX (Ship Complete or Don't Ship).

options.title: Sovereign Design System & Generative Component Library
options.description: The Creative Liberation Engine will develop and maintain its own comprehensive, internal design system (tokens, guidelines, patterns) and a corresponding generative component library. AURORA will define the design principles and component specifications, KEEPER will store them, and BOLT will be responsible for generating code based on these components. This ensures complete ownership and control over the visual language and interactive elements of all Creative Liberation Engine-generated UIs.
options.tradeoffs: Pros: Complete sovereignty (Article I), high consistency across all generated UIs, robust foundation for future innovation. Cons: Significant initial development effort to build the design system and component library from scratch. May initially be slower than leveraging existing external frameworks.
options.architecture: AURORA defines design tokens and component APIs. KEEPER stores the design system specifications. BOLT implements a code generation engine that translates high-level UI descriptions into actual component code using the internal library. A robust versioning and update mechanism for the design system is crucial.
options.design: A unique, branded Creative Liberation Engine visual identity will be established. Focus on atomic design principles, accessibility standards (WCAG 2.1 AA), responsive design patterns, and a clear information hierarchy. The design system will include guidelines for typography, color palettes, spacing, iconography, and motion.

options.title: AI-Driven Visual Language Generation & Refinement
options.description: Instead of a fixed design system, the Creative Liberation Engine will use advanced AI models (primarily within AURORA) to dynamically generate and refine visual languages and UI components based on high-level textual or conceptual prompts. This allows for greater flexibility and adaptation to diverse contexts and aesthetic requirements. VERA will validate the generated designs against established aesthetic and usability metrics.
options.tradeoffs: Pros: Highly adaptable, capable of generating diverse and novel designs, potentially faster iteration on new styles. Cons: Requires sophisticated AI models and extensive training data. Risk of generating inconsistent or aesthetically suboptimal designs if not properly constrained and validated.
options.architecture: AURORA integrates generative AI models (e.g., GANs, diffusion models) trained on vast datasets of high-quality UI/UX designs. These models take conceptual inputs and output design tokens, component structures, and even raw CSS/SVG. VERA implements a design evaluation framework using metrics for aesthetics, usability, and constitutional compliance (e.g., accessibility).
options.design: Focus on the 'taste' and 'style' parameters of the AI. The system should learn to produce designs that are not only functional but also visually appealing and aligned with modern design trends or specific brand guidelines. This could include exploring glassmorphism, neumorphism, brutalism, or minimalist aesthetics as directed.

options.title: Semantic UI Assembly Engine
options.description: The Creative Liberation Engine will focus on understanding the semantic intent behind UI requirements. RELAY or SIGNAL will process high-level semantic descriptions of data and user interactions. AURORA will then interpret these semantics to intelligently assemble appropriate UI components and layouts from an internal, semantically tagged component library (managed by KEEPER). BOLT generates the final code.
options.tradeoffs: Pros: Highly efficient for data-driven UIs, ensures strong information hierarchy, aligns UI with user intent. Cons: Less flexible for highly artistic or abstract design requirements. Requires a robust semantic understanding layer.
options.architecture: Develop a sophisticated natural language understanding (NLU) module within AURORA to parse semantic UI requirements. KEEPER maintains a library of UI components tagged with their semantic meaning and usage context. AURORA then uses a rule-based or machine learning approach to select and arrange these components.
options.design: Emphasize clarity, functionality, and effective communication of information. The design will inherently follow the structure of the content. This approach lends itself well to dashboards, data visualizations, forms, and content-heavy landing pages where the primary goal is clear information delivery.

options.title: Context-Aware Adaptive Layout System
options.description: The Creative Liberation Engine will build an internal system that dynamically adapts UI layouts and component styling based on real-time context (e.g., device type, screen size, user preferences, accessibility needs, data availability). AURORA will be responsible for the adaptive logic, and IRIS will manage the runtime adjustments. This ensures optimal user experience across a multitude of environments.
options.tradeoffs: Pros: Superior user experience across devices and contexts, inherently accessible and responsive. Cons: Increased architectural complexity for dynamic layout generation and runtime adaptation. Requires comprehensive context sensing and decision-making capabilities.
options.architecture: Implement a robust context-sensing module (potentially part of SIGNAL or RELAY). AURORA develops algorithms for dynamic layout generation and component adaptation based on contextual inputs. IRIS orchestrates the rendering and re-rendering of UI elements in real-time. This includes responsive breakpoints, flexible grids, and adaptive component states.
options.design: Focus on fluid, resilient, and accessible designs. Visual elements will gracefully adjust to different screen sizes and orientations. Typography, spacing, and image scaling will be responsive. The system will support dark mode/light mode, high contrast, and other user accessibility preferences seamlessly.

options.title: Gamified Design System Evolution
options.description: Introduce a gamified feedback loop for the Creative Liberation Engine's internal design system. Agents (or agent simulations) will 'play-test' generated UIs, providing qualitative and quantitative feedback on aesthetics, usability, and performance. VERA will validate this feedback, and AURORA will use it to iteratively evolve and improve the design system and generative capabilities.
options.tradeoffs: Pros: Continuous improvement of design output, self-correcting system, aligns with zero human wait time by automating design evaluation. Cons: Requires sophisticated simulation and evaluation agents. Defining objective metrics for 'beauty' and 'usability' for AI is challenging.
options.architecture: Develop a 'simulation environment' where generated UIs can be rendered and interacted with by agent-simulators (e.g., COMET for UI interaction). VERA develops a suite of evaluation metrics (e.g., eye-tracking simulations, click-through rates, task completion times, aesthetic scores based on learned preferences). This data forms a reward signal for AURORA's design generation models.
options.design: The system will learn to optimize for user engagement, aesthetic appeal, and task efficiency. This could lead to the evolution of novel interaction patterns and visual styles that are proven effective through simulated user testing.
